title: Integrator applications are handled centrally today but will route exclusively through Prime Agents long term
content:
A.2.2.4.1.2.1 describes the interim arrangement: "In the near term, applications are made directly to Operational GovOps," which must maintain a Sky Forum thread for Integrator Applications, review applications, coordinate with interested Prime Agents, and issue Reward Codes to approved applicants. The applicant list is Active Data under Operational GovOps' Direct Edit control (A.2.2.4.1.2.1.1).

A.2.2.4.1.2.2 states the destination: "In the long term, Integrator applications come exclusively through Prime Agents. Prime Agents may establish whatever processes they deem appropriate to receive inbound requests for potential partnerships."

The migration is from a **single reviewed queue** to **many unstandardized front doors**. Note what is and is not delegated. Intake and process design pass to Prime Agents; the Integrator Requirements themselves (alignment per A.2.2.4.1.1.1, legal compliance per A.2.2.4.1.1.2) remain Atlas-level, and A.2.2.4.1.3.1 keeps the Reward Code issuance decision with Operational GovOps — which "may contract with another actor" to perform that review.

So the pattern is: decentralize sourcing, retain gatekeeping. Prime Agents compete to find Integrators, while the ability to make an Integrator economically real stays with a central issuer. Volume scales with the number of Agents; approval standards do not fragment with it.
description: The near-term path runs through Operational GovOps with a Forum thread and issued Reward Codes; the long-term design removes central intake entirely and lets each Prime Agent set its own process.
